title: Runtime Analysis and Asymptotics in C
subtitle: Trace, count, sum, simplify, classify, and prove.
description: A cumulative runtime-analysis course covering exact frequency counts, loop sums, asymptotic notation, formal proofs, recurrences, space, and amortized analysis.

moduleRange.label: Runtime Analysis and Asymptotics in C

prerequisites: Comfort tracing loops and function calls.
intendedFor: Learners following the cumulative C data-structures and algorithms pathway.
learningGoals: Derive exact execution-count functions.
Classify growth using O, Ω, and Θ.
Solve recursive recurrences by substitution and trees.
Prove bounds and state all assumptions.

courseOverview.recommendedSequence: Follow modules in order. Each standard module extends the same cumulative workspace and ends with a module project. The final module is one cumulative capstone topic.
courseOverview.summary: A cumulative runtime-analysis course covering exact frequency counts, loop sums, asymptotic notation, formal proofs, recurrences, space, and amortized analysis.

moduleSummary.title: Frequency Counting in C
moduleSummary.coreSkill: Turn executed C statements into exact frequency tables and time functions.
moduleSummary.outputFocus: Add an operation-counting report to the analysis workspace.

moduleSummary.title: Asymptotics with Limits
moduleSummary.coreSkill: Move from exact functions to formal growth comparisons using limits and case assumptions.
moduleSummary.outputFocus: Add growth comparison and reporting functions.

moduleSummary.title: Proofs from the Definitions
moduleSummary.coreSkill: Turn observed growth into explicit constants and thresholds from asymptotic definitions.

moduleSummary.title: Recurrence Relations
moduleSummary.coreSkill: Derive and solve recurrences from recursive code using substitution and recursion trees.
moduleSummary.outputFocus: Add recurrence tracing and level reports.

moduleSummary.title: Applied Cost Analysis
moduleSummary.coreSkill: Apply exact, asymptotic, space, and amortized analysis to data-structure operations.

moduleSummary.title: Runtime Analysis Capstone
moduleSummary.coreSkill: Complete the full trace-count-sum-simplify-classify-prove workflow on unfamiliar C code.
moduleSummary.outputFocus: Analyze a multi-function C program from source code to exact time functions, recurrences, space costs, and formal asymptotic proofs.

authoringGuidance: This course must always use subjectSlug c, courseSlug c-runtime-analysis-asymptotics, profileId c, and the shared C multi-file workspace policy.
Teach the idea in language-neutral pseudocode before showing the complete C implementation.
Use pseudocode_input for algorithm completion, reorder, trace, or full-write activities; never validate raw prose by exact string matching.
Validate pseudocode through normalized structure rules and deterministic trace scenarios. AI may explain failures but is not the primary pass/fail checker.
Every pointer-heavy, recursive, tree, heap, sorting, or graph operation begins with a manual algorithm_animation using stable layouts and one state change per frame.
Place a predict-next-step interaction before important animation transitions.
Every C code_input uses fixedLanguage c, recipeType fixed_tests, entryFilePath main.c, and complete starterFiles and solutionFiles.
Keep learner TODOs in named implementation .c files and preserve supplied headers and deterministic main.c harnesses.
Compile all authored .c files as C11 and free official-solution allocations before exit.
Complexity is graded with counts, choices, traces, or structured pseudocode—not exact Big-O prose.
Every standard module ends with one progressive module project; the final module contains exactly one cumulative capstone topic.

animationRules: Use previous, next, play or pause, replay, and a visible step counter.
Keep layouts stable; animate links, active cells, call frames, or edges rather than moving the whole structure.
Synchronize heap tree and array states, recursion and call stack states, and graph state with queue or stack state.
Prefer five to ten meaningful frames and one state transition per frame.
pseudocodeRules: Use dialect zoeskoul-v1 and inputKind pseudocode_input.
Accept equivalent variable names and harmless syntax variants after normalization.
Require explicit termination, state updates, and invariant-preserving branches.
Use structure plus scenario execution for pass/fail.
Keep the learner pseudocode visible beside the following C translation exercise.
workspaceRules: Reuse the same course workspace across module projects.
Do not ask learners to create boilerplate files or remember compiler commands.
Each new module adds focused .h/.c files while preserving prior passing tests.
Project steps are progressive and may not reset earlier work.

assessmentAndDelivery.recommendedRhythm: Two or three traced lessons plus one hands-on implementation session each week.
assessmentAndDelivery.closingNote: Learners complete Runtime Analysis and Asymptotics in C with an executable cumulative project and an analysis record.
